claims.text: The Frauenkirche, officially known as the Dom zu Unserer Lieben Frau, is a late Gothic brick church that serves as the cathedral of the Archdiocese of Munich and Freising.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Construction of the church began in 1468 under the direction of architect Jörg von Halsbach, and the main building was completed in only 20 years.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Brick was chosen as the primary building material because there were no stone quarries nearby and for financial reasons.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The original design called for pointed Gothic spires on top of the towers, but they were never built due to a lack of money.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The towers remained unfinished until 1525, when they were topped with the distinctive domes that now define the Munich skyline.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The design of the characteristic domes atop the towers may have been modelled after the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The two towers are almost equal in height, with the north tower measuring 98.57 meters and the south tower 98.45 meters.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: A widespread local legend incorrectly claims that the two towers differ in height by exactly one meter.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: To preserve the city's skyline, local laws and a 2004 plebiscite prohibit the construction of any building in the city center taller than 99 meters.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Eleven kings and archdukes of Bavaria are interred within the church.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Inside the entrance of the church is a black mark resembling a footprint, known as the Teufelstritt (Devil's Footstep).
claims.subject: self

claims.text: According to legend, the Devil stomped his foot furiously at the entrance after realizing the builder had cleverly positioned columns to hide the church's windows from that spot.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Another version of the legend claims that the wind blowing around the church was left behind by the Devil when he stormed away in anger.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The church suffered severe damage from air raids during World War II, and its final stage of restoration was completed in 1994.
claims.subject: self
